clue.text: One scene in 25 worked with Auden

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Sherwood Forest, Robin Hood's haunt, lies in Nottinghamshire, the answer to 25

explanation.surface: A setting in the Midlands county where someone collaborated with the poet Auden.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: Christopher Isherwood co-wrote plays with W. H. Auden in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood, the novelist, was W. H. Auden's friend and collaborator on several verse plays.

clue.text: Singers, when one is out of order, shed in 19?

parts.note: a choir is a body of singers
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A choir with one member out of step sheds something in a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the I of CHOIR to the front gives the new word. 19 is DEICIDE, the killing of a god.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this ethereal fluid flowed in gods' veins in place of blood, so it is what killing a god would spill.

clue.text: Boy poet takes most of 26 from geranium

indicators.note: from signals that one set of letters is taken out of the other

parts.note: herb Robert is a common wild geranium

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final pair of letters dropped

parts.note: 26 across is ROBIN

explanation.surface: A lad who writes verse picks a bird's name out of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... from' signals removal: take ROB (ROBIN less IN) out of HERB ROBERT. George Herbert was a seventeenth-century poet, and Herbert is also a boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Herbert was a metaphysical poet, and the name doubles as an ordinary boy's first name.

clue.text: Veto letters being taken from true love by government

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are removed from the pair of words that follow, leaving the rest

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blocks the post being sent from a sweetheart by official order.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove V, E, T and O from TRUELOVE and R, U, L, E are left, in that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule is the exercise of governing authority, so government and rule are synonyms.

clue.text: Authorised resistance?

electrical resistance is measured in units named after Georg Ohm

explanation.surface: An approved opposition, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters stand for On Her Majesty's Service, an official sanction, and they also spell the units of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Rough border to the last in underfloor shelf

indicators.note: in a down clue the shelf comes under the floor

parts.note: a deck is a floor, as on a ship

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the shelf

explanation.walkthrough: 'underfloor' is read as 'under floor': LEDGE goes below DECK. 'the last' is E, put in LEDGE to make LEEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckle edge is the ragged untrimmed border of handmade paper.

clue.text: Numbers (including verses) make a connection

definitions.note: the definition names what the device does: it is the thing that makes a connection between computers

indicators.note: including means the numbers hold the verses inside them

parts.note: MM is a number in Roman numerals, two thousand
an ode is a poem, a set of verses

explanation.surface: Numbers with poems added link things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is the device that connects a computer to a network over a line.

clue.text: Reportedly forced, become husband to an inamorata of 26

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by how they are spoken

explanation.surface: Under compulsion, so they say, a man weds the beloved of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, MADE MARRY AN sounds like the name of Robin Hood's sweetheart; 26 is ROBIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's sweetheart in the legends, so she is the beloved of the 26 answer.

clue.text: Money is said to breed sorrows

indicators.note: is said means the word for money is heard rather than read

parts.note: dollars are money

explanation.surface: The proverbial claim that wealth brings grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to breed' is linking: money, spoken, gives sorrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolours is a literary word for griefs or sorrows.

clue.text: His range in 25

parts.note: his means the man's
a field is a range, as in field of vision

explanation.surface: A man's territory in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Mansfield is a town in Nottinghamshire, the answer to 25.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a market town lying within Nottinghamshire.

clue.text: Injury confines former student in European football club, one with Devonshire connections

indicators.note: confines means the injury holds the next word inside it

parts.note: harm is injury
old means former

indicators.note: in puts the student inside the club

parts.note: AC Milan is an Italian football club
L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A hurt keeps an old pupil at a Continental club, someone linked to Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Macmillan married Lady Dorothy Cavendish, daughter of the Duke of Devonshire. Devonshire refers to the dukedom, not the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Macmillan, British Prime Minister 1957-63, was son-in-law of the ninth Duke of Devonshire.

clue.text: Bank that may be taken in

definitions.meaning: a ridge of rock or sand just under the sea's surface
a sail's folded section that sailors take in to shorten sail in high wind

explanation.surface: A riverside slope that can be absorbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is an underwater bank, and to reef a sail is to take part of it in.

clue.text: Pudding choice no good?

parts.note: plum as an adjective means choice, the best
duff is British slang for useless, no good

explanation.surface: Picking a dessert that turns out badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a boiled suet pudding with dried fruit.

clue.text: Dent made by sniper does damage

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dent caused by a marksman's shot that wrecks something.

explanation.definitionFit: A depression is a hollow or dent in a surface.

clue.text: It means severe frost in employment held by power

indicators.note: held by means the employed phrase sits inside the power

parts.note: might is power
in use means employed

explanation.surface: A hard freeze while working under authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus eight degrees is a temperature well below freezing, a hard frost.

clue.text: 8, writer with a broken heart, in stock

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the stock

parts.note: kine is an old word for cattle, livestock

indicators.note: broken means the letters of heart are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer with a broken heart in the stocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the heart, which then sits in the cattle. 8 is MANSFIELD: Katherine Mansfield, the New Zealand short-story writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Katherine Mansfield was a celebrated short-story writer, so her first name with 8 names her.

clue.text: Cook general?

definitions.meaning: someone who works in a kitchen
Lord ..., the British field marshal of the First World War recruiting poster

explanation.surface: A military commander who can cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchener is a kitchen worker or cook, and Kitchener was a famous British general.

clue.text: Say tea with cider?

Cider with ... is Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswold childhood

explanation.surface: Ordering a drink alongside some cider.

clue.text: Underground railway opened by Murphy?

parts.note: the Tube is London's Underground

explanation.surface: A Tube line opened by someone called Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato, from its Irish associations; 'opened by' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato, nicknamed a murphy, is a swollen underground stem, a tuber.

clue.text: Bighead was in charge but went back for a dip

parts.note: the head of Big is its first letter, B
ran means was in charge, as in ran a company

indicators.note: went back means the word but is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An egotistic boss retreated to go for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a lucky dip at a British fete: prizes buried in bran for children to dig out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bran tub is a lucky dip, a tub of bran with prizes hidden in it.

clue.text: Indiscreet guru dead 'n' desecrated

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Settle round one that makes immortal mortal

indicators.note: round means the settling word goes around the one

parts.note: to decide is to settle
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.definitionFit: Deicide is the killing of a god, which turns an immortal into a mortal.

clue.text: Executioners effect end with shame

indicators.note: effect, as a verb meaning bring about, signals the letters being worked into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hangmen bring about a disgraceful finish.

clue.text: Speaker with 8 for silk

Michael Mansfield is a well-known QC, a silk; 8 is MANSFIELD

explanation.surface: An orator and a famous lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a senior barrister (Queen's or King's Counsel), from the silk gown worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike is a microphone, used by a speaker, and Mike Mansfield is a prominent British barrister.

clue.text: English getting flu, say? It happens

explanation.surface: An Englishman catching influenza, apparently.

clue.text: Put car after 8

definitions.meaning: Mansfield ... is Jane Austen's novel; 8 is MANSFIELD

explanation.surface: Leaving the car after eight o'clock.

clue.text: Quasi-autonomous part of the East

indicators.note: part of means the letters are taken from inside the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: A semi-independent region in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent loosely called the East.

clue.text: No teetotallers here!

clue.text: How to win an election if you don't stand?

definitions.text: How to win an election if you don't stand?
